session: This round was opened by the SESSION as M0-a-06's HARDENING ROUND S11 (J237 (2): the M0 hardening phase's fix rounds, batched per owning item; J238: M0 is the bedrock — the default for an M0 row is FIX with an exact precaution and a pin; J567: the bar is an independent closing check's PASS on the evidence), on THE CONTRACTS ROUND's kernel rows (J800 (3)): RL13 (queue Q205; the inventory's L26) — a batch's refusal names the body it refused — and RL15 (queue Q135) — the gate plan's dry run — with the leg's NO-SHIFT. Each 'failing line' below is one such row — an open queue row routed to this item (docs/M0-FIX-QUEUE.md) or a row the item's latest closing check wrote into its notes file; its evidence names the SOURCE you MUST read whole before fixing; the fix shape and the pin are the session's reading, binding unless the source or the code shows it wrong — then say so in your notes and do what the finding needs. THE RULES OF A HARDENING ROUND: (1) inside the item's owns and nowhere else — a row that needs another item's file is REPORTED, not built; FOR THIS ROUND the seats write inside THE WRITE SCOPE: M0-a-06's owns (plat/packages/kernel/src/tx/ and plat/packages/kernel/test/tx/, unchanged in M0-work.json) plus THE CROSS-ITEM SCOPE (LEG 1's OWN TEXT below); wherever this brief or plat/docs/build/M0.md §3 says 'inside the item's owns', read 'inside the write scope'; a change any other file would need, or any other change in a scope file, is REPORTED, not built; (2) every row gets a PIN (a test that is red without the fix; your mutant table shows each pin killing its mutant) unless the row is comment-only or asks for a choices row — then the text is the deliverable; (3) BEHAVIOUR: a hardening fix may move output where a defect is fixed — a DECLARED shift, stated in your choices row with the before and after (digests and goldens re-recorded in the same round, named), never silent; where a row offers alternatives, take the one the design's text supports and say which; a change of an operation's or stage's CONTRACT (its design-level behaviour, a record or file format, an exported API) is NOT yours — report it as a note for the session's ruling and leave the row at REPORTED; (4) J264 / N-58: the refusal census of the item's registered families before and after the round, never rising (a row whose fix makes a lawful input succeed lowers it and says so); (5) API frozen (J263 Q1): no export of a folder index or the barrel added, removed or renamed unless a row explicitly asks for one — then the index change is the row's and stated; message texts pinned verbatim where a row changes one (J263 Q6); (6) the gates, NEAR and RELATED@1000 as the brief above says, at W=1; (7) the item's notes file gains a section 'Hardening round S11' with the row-by-row outcome (fixed / pinned / reported, each with its evidence and mutant), and the round's choices row names every row it closes. The CLOSING CHECKER confirms every row's outcome with its own evidence (re-reading the source note or queue row), re-kills every pin's mutant, re-measures the refusal census, and judges new findings by the blocker rule only; a row left REPORTED with a stated contract reason is not a failing line. THIS IS LEG 1 OF A MERGED ROUND OF THREE LEGS — THE CONTRACTS ROUND (the MERGED-ROUND RULE, J443): M0-a-06 S11 → M0-e-03 S6 → M0-c-04 S8, in that order, on ONE tree and ONE branch, no reset between, each leg with its own build, closing check, LANDED line and record; leg 2 launches only when leg 1 returned ok with check.verdict pass (it builds on it); leg 3 builds on leg 1 and on nothing of leg 2 (their write scopes share no file and no package), so it launches when leg 1 passed and leg 2 has RETURNED, whatever leg 2's verdict [SESSION: confirm or strike this clause at binding — the draft's open question 2]. THE ROUND CARRIES NO LEG OF M0-a-05: the queue rows' 'a-05' (Q205 'the field in insert/'; Q135 (a) 'M0-a-05's insert/') is corrected by the code — the refusal that names a body is made by the transaction at commit (kernel/src/tx/tx.ts roleProblems → run → reject), and a plan that commits nothing for a SEQUENCE of splits is a dry run, which only tx/ can open and undo (docs/validation/a05-contracts-spec-2026-11-13/draft.md §0, §1.1, §1.3 (c)). RULINGS BINDING (each read by its own grep, never the 1.3 MB file whole: grep '^| J637 ', '^| J648 ', '^| J800 ', '^| J263 ', '^| J264 ', '^| J238 ' docs/PROGRESS.md; and grep 'RL13\|RL15' docs/validation/hardening-retriage-2026-11-09/plan.md): RL13 (J637 (3); plan.md's ruling row): a STRUCTURED FIELD on the kernel's refusal naming the refused body — YES, ADDITIVE — the refusal codes and detail texts unchanged; M0-e-03 reads it in its following touch (queue Q205). RL15 (J648; plan.md's ruling row; queue Q135): the always-rejected planning batch of S5a's gate plan is removed by the kernel's plan that commits nothing — seam (a), in the form the session ruled after this spec's review: the kernel's DRY RUN (`dryRun` in tx/tx.ts, `Kernel.dryRun` on the façade) [SESSION: the ruled form is filled at binding]. J800 (2)–(3): Q135 stays M0's (J238 (1)) and is bound with RL13 into THE CONTRACTS ROUND, specced with its adversarial review. J263: Q1 — the API is frozen: no export of a folder index or of the barrel is added, removed or renamed by this round (the new types and functions are read BY PATH; the public surface that changes is the `Kernel` interface's `tx` return type and its new `dryRun` member, which RL13 / RL15 rule); Q6 — every pinned message text stays verbatim. J264: zero refusals of lawful input — the refusal census of the item's registered families before and after, never rising. J238 (1)–(3): nothing is carried, narrowed or waived for pace. THIS SPEC TOOK ITS ADVERSARIAL REVIEW (J631 (2) (a): a contract between items): [SESSION: the review's path, its findings and the rulings file that answers them are named here at binding; where a line below and the rulings file disagree, the rulings file binds and the seat says so in its notes]. THE DRAFT this entry was cut from (docs/validation/a05-contracts-spec-2026-11-13/draft.md) is evidence, never binding over this entry. THE GATE: the round opens on the design head AFTER M0-a-06 S10 (the RQ2 round's second leg, which edits tx/) has landed; it reads nothing of the router round (M0-a-05 S14 – S16: insert/insertChain.ts, insert/stretch.ts, insert/snapRound.ts) and writes no file of it. Every cite below was read on the design head 102ff939 (insert/ on origin/wip/child-a05s14 @ 9354851f): re-read every cite on your tree; the files, functions and forms named are binding, the line numbers are not. DECLARED REDS OF THE HEAD, never a failing line (brought to the head of 2026-11-13; where THE MEASURED LIST above names a red of the head differently, this list is the newer): Q152's six M0-a-09 bands tests; J176's Mac-reference bench tests (bench/test/calibrate, host, timing); bench/test/site/summary.test.ts's canary (J772 (7): the committed site summary is stale until the session's re-run — the compose.test.ts and spike.test.ts reds the measured list names beside it were re-pinned since by M0-e-06 S4 and are green); Q153's flake (testkit/test/determinism/dilation.test.ts; re-run alone); and Q202 — the seven 'later rungs' cases of packages/layout/test/enceinte/s5seeds.test.ts, which register only at FULL strength (PLAT_FUZZ_RUNS unset; at 1 000 runs the file reports 'No test found') and are red there since before this round was specced: another item's, re-pinned by a round in flight. THE RESTARTS (a fact of this platform on 2026-11-12 / 13: a container restarts about every two hours whether or not background tasks are live; /home/user/maps-scratch survives, every process dies, /tmp does not survive): every run over ten minutes is a STEP OF A RE-ENTRANT CHAIN under /home/user/maps-scratch/waves/ — its log and its exit-code file beside it, and for a run of many parts one exit-code file per part, so that a seat that comes back after a restart skips what is finished: the census one file per seed or family; RELATED@1000 IN CHUNKS — collect RELATED's own file list once (`vitest related --run` with the JSON reporter and a test-name filter that matches nothing, e.g. -t '^__no_such_test__$'), split it by 12 files, run each chunk with `vitest run --passWithNoTests` at PLAT_FUZZ_RUNS=1000 under ONE recorded PLAT_FUZZ_SEED, each chunk's JSON report and exit code beside it, the totals summed from the JSON reports (a file that registers no test at 1 000 runs is named); NEAR one run per project; each mutant its own exit-code file. A CHECKPOINT line names the chain's directory and its next unfinished step at least every twenty minutes of the seat's own work. No timing bar is judged on these machines. THE SEATS: the session's tiers for a kernel item (J390 / J631 / J714), named at launch; the CLOSING CHECK is the STRONGER checker's — this leg changes SOURCE. THE WAITING RULE and the waiter as the brief above says. LEG 1's OWN TEXT. THE CROSS-ITEM SCOPE (RL13, RL15; M0-a-16 lends): plat/packages/kernel/src/facade/types.ts — the `Kernel` interface's `tx` member's return type (TxResult), the new `dryRun` member beside it, and their path imports; plat/packages/kernel/src/facade/kernel.ts — runTx's two type annotations (type only) and the `dryRun` member built beside `tx` in createKernel; nothing else in either file. The façade's new member is tested from kernel/test/tx/ (a test may build a kernel with createKernel); kernel/test/facade/ is read and run, never edited. The scope's mechanics are M0-a-06 S9's entry's (the base mirror; THE SCOPE DIFF per scope file with its SHA-256s; the record claims tx/ and test/tx/ only; the CLOSING CHECKER confirms the scope by landed:verify's expected mismatch for M0-a-16 alone and by reverse-applying the diff); at the landing the SESSION re-lands M0-a-16's record through tools/session/land_child.py. THE DECLARED SHIFT: NONE — LINE 3 shows it: no refusal code or detail text changes, no committed path changes, and a refusal other than the commit's role-consistency refusal carries no new property. THE ORDER OF WORK: LINE 1, LINE 2, then LINE 3 on the final sources. THE LIST FOR THE SESSION'S SEAMS (written in the notes, never edited here): kernel/API.md — §5 'The failure contract' (the field), §7's `Kernel` block (the `tx` signature, :443 and :463 on 102ff939, and the new `dryRun` member); the design text §3.3 (a batch's refusal and its key; the dry run) for the amendments' next apply pass; queue rows Q205 and Q135 (their 'a-05' wording); C-0285 (2) and C-0452 (10) (leg 3's choices row supersedes their planning sentence); any other item's test that pins a tx refusal object whole and moves, and any type error the widened `Kernel['tx']` raises in another package (owner, file, test or line, before, after). Notes section 'Hardening round S11'; verdict plat/docs/build/checks/M0-a-06-s11.md; lanes build/M0-a-06-fix-s11 / check/M0-a-06-close-s11 (no key of them in docs/lane-events.log at this writing; re-keyed by the session if one appears); ledger ids the next free at build time.

lines.required_change: BUILD (RL13's shape, draft §2.1): tx/types.ts declares `TxResult<T> = Extract<KernelResult<T>, { ok: true }> | (Extract<KernelResult<T>, { ok: false }> & { readonly refused?: RoleKey })`, its doc comment saying where the key is set and that every other refusal lacks it; NO line in tx/index.ts or the barrel (J263 Q1) — the façade imports it by path. roleProblems returns its problems with their keys (`{ detail, key: { role, entity, ordinal } }`, each detail BYTE-IDENTICAL, the order unchanged); run keeps ONE problems list in today's order (the other sources' strings carried as `{ detail }`) and refuses with `problems[0].detail` and `problems[0].key`; reject takes the optional key and returns `{ ok: false, code, detail, refused: key }` when one is given, otherwise exactly `err(code, detail)` — NO `refused` property, not even undefined; tx()'s return type, and through the cross-item scope facade/types.ts `tx` and runTx's annotations, are `TxResult<Committed<T | KernelResult<unknown>[]>>`. No other refusal sets a key: the op and callback paths do not pass on a key their result carried [SESSION: Q5], nor do failures, the repair path, the work limit, levelProblems, clearanceProblems, checkIndexBatch or env.invariants. PINS (kernel/test/tx/, a new file): (P1) a callback batch inserting a shore ring that branches at commit (the slow-rings construction: rings of one `('shore', body)` welded by attraction) is refused E_INVARIANT with its detail byte-equal to today's and `refused` deep-equal `{ role: 'shore', entity: <body>, ordinal: 0 }`; the same for a way (reentry.test.ts:306's `(way, way:c1)`) and for a wall; (P2) a batch with TWO branching keys carries the key its detail prints — the first of the record's role keys; (P3) `'refused' in r` is false for a callback refusal, a declared op's refusal, E_WORK_LIMIT, an expect class floor, a level-consistency refusal and an index-freshness refusal (each constructed or taken from tx's existing tests); (P4) through createKernel's façade the caller receives the same key and text. MUTANTS: M1 reject drops the key (P1 red); M2 the key of the last problem or the last role key (P2 red); M3 every E_INVARIANT carries the batch's first role key (P3 red); M4 a detail text changed by one character (P1 and every message pin red); M5 the ordinal hard-coded 0 — if no linear role is indexed (arena/roles.json), say so and drop M5. lines.line: LINE 2 — RL15 (Q135; c-04 S4's N-10; J648): S5a plans its gate vertices in a batch that is always rejected (layout/src/growth/boundary.ts traceStage: `kernel.tx(l1Spec(arena, STAGES.S5), (o) => { … return err('E_INVARIANT', 'S5a: the gate plan (a batch always rejected)'); })`) because the strategy needs the gate points before its batch opens and only the kernel's split places them; every watcher of `tx` counts it as a refused S5 batch. lines.required_change: BUILD (RL15's shape, draft §2.2 (a-2)): tx/tx.ts exports `dryRun<T>(p: Plat, spec: KernelTx, fn: (overlay: Overlay) => KernelResult<T>, env: TxEnv = {}): KernelResult<T>` — the callback form only (`spec.ops` empty) and `spec.expect` empty, both asserted; `open(p, spec, env)` with every check of it; `fn` on the overlay; then, WHATEVER `fn` returned, the batch undone to its frame (`undoBatch`) and closed; E_WORK_LIMIT (`workDetail`) when `overWork`, else `fn`'s result as it returned it; no commit row, no record, no `onCommit`, neither the version nor the restore generation moved; a throw undone and rethrown as `tx` rethrows (`rethrown`, its form 'dry'). Read BY PATH by the façade; no index or barrel line (J263 Q1). The façade (cross-item scope): `Kernel` gains `dryRun<T>(tx: KernelTx, fn: (overlay: Overlay) => KernelResult<T>): KernelResult<T>`, built in createKernel as runTx builds `tx` for a callback — the overlay this kernel's open transaction inside (`within`), the frame pushed and popped, every value stamped `{ key, version: -1 }` as a rejected batch's (C-0220 (3)) — its doc: 'a plan that commits nothing: never a batch, seen by no `tx` watcher (RL15)'. PINS (kernel/test/tx/): (P1) a dry run that splits an edge through `kernel.geom.splitThrough` returns the new vertex's point, and afterwards the arena's version, restore generation, level digests, slot counters, index (the frame observer's oracle, installFrameObserver) and tables are as before, and a counting `onCommit` was not called; (P2) a `tx` batch run right after makes the same split at the same slot as with no dry run before it; (P3) a dry run over its work limit returns E_WORK_LIMIT, undone; (P4) a dry run inside an open batch on the same arena throws 'another batch is open on this arena'; one with ops or expect rows throws; (P5) a writer handed the dry run's overlay after it returned throws (closed), and in the debug build a slot value it returned fails `assertCurrent`; (P6) a throw inside `fn` is rethrown with the `tx …/dry/…` prefix, the arena untouched; (P7) through the façade a `tx` wrapper in base.ts `watched`'s pattern sees no batch for a dry run. MUTANTS: M1 dryRun commits (P1, P7 red); M2 the index log left open or not undone (P1's oracle); M3 the slot counters not restored (P2); M4 no work limit (P3); M5 the closed flag not set (P5); M6 the façade's member without `within` (a geom writer inside refuses: P1 red); M7 the façade stamps the result current (P5).
